This document translates the first-class style and layout design into a runtime architecture that preserves CRC's immediate-mode Canvas model. It defines the responsibilities and execution seams needed for a rapid, incremental implementation. Exact source filenames may change during planning, but the boundaries and data flow are architectural commitments unless the design is amended.
CRC currently renders synchronously and depth first on a scheduled animation frame:
1. Invoke a component function.
2. Let that component paint immediately.
3. Traverse the elements it returned in source order.
4. Restore Canvas and runtime state after the subtree.

Component elements already exist before invocation as lightweight descriptors containing a function and props. This is sufficient for declared layout. CRC does not need to record paths, pixels, or drawing commands into a retained display list.
The architecture must preserve:
- one live CRC mount per Canvas;
- requestAnimationFrame update coalescing;
- parent-path, function, key, and occurrence identity rules;
- Canvas save/restore isolation;
- source paint order and reverse-paint-order logical targeting;
- accumulated transforms and clips shared by drawing and interaction;
- layer ownership and global target ordering;
- fail-closed resource cleanup.
The element descriptor gains first-class style metadata:

ts type ReservedElementKey = "key" | "style"; type UnionKeys = T extends unknown ? keyof T : never; type ProgramProps

= 0 extends 1 & P ? P : Extract, ReservedElementKey> extends never ? P : never; interface CompEl { type: CompType; props: ProgramProps

; style: Readonly; key?: string; }
The public component call remains a single ergonomic object with reserved `style` and `key` fields. `defineComp` separates those fields from programmatic props when it creates the descriptor:

ts const Card = defineComp<CardProps, CardStyle>((props, style, ctx) => { // props: data, callbacks, and other programmatic inputs // style: normalized/resolved visual values for this render }); Card({ value: 42, onSelect, style: { width: "100%", minHeight: 120 }, });

`style` defaults to an empty object where a component supports complete defaults. Required visual inputs remain required by that component's style type. The factory input expresses that rule structurally:

ts type RequiredKeys<T> = T extends unknown ? { [K in keyof T]-?: Pick<T, K> extends Required<Pick<T, K>> ? K : never; }[keyof T] : never; type StyleField<S> = [RequiredKeys<S>] extends [never] ? { style?: S } : { style: S };

Both checks distribute over unions: one reserved prop member invalidates the whole program-props declaration, and one required style member makes `style` required. Every component-specific style type must explicitly extend `SystemStyle` or intersect with it. This is a positive style-schema contract, not a blacklist: unrelated arrays, functions, dates, URLs, errors, blobs, buffers, matrices, and arbitrary resource/class types fail structurally unless their declared type deliberately opts in. `SystemStyle` retains only optional `custom` and has no index signature, so declared style schemas remain closed and excess-property checked. Ordinary inputs do not need to spell `custom` when the declared target style has another matching member.

`defineComp` rejects program-prop declarations containing reserved `key` or `style`; the descriptor owns those values and component code cannot read them through props. Calls without an own `key` or `style` retain the exact program props object; calls with either metadata field take the extraction path and store a separate props object. No public API supports visual values in both props and style.
Style types are capability intersections, not a global index signature:

ts interface BoxStyle { /* size and constraint participation */ } interface TransformStyle { /* transform values */ } interface PaintStyle { /* fill, stroke, opacity */ } interface FlexContainerStyle { /* flex container values */ } interface LayoutItemStyle { /* optional absolute, overlay, flex, and grid participation values */ } interface RectStyle extends SystemStyle, BoxStyle, TransformStyle, PaintStyle, LayoutItemStyle { x?: Exclude<Length, "auto">; y?: Exclude<Length, "auto">; width: Length; height: Length; custom?: Record<string, unknown>; }
The implementation distinguishes:
- **Specified style:** immutable author input stored on the element.
- **Normalized style:** parsed values, expanded shorthands, and component defaults with no parent-derived geometry.
- **Resolved style:** finite values for the current containing box and layout allocation, passed to the render function.
There is no cascade or inherited-style stage.

Normalization is owned by focused style modules. Layout-independent paint normalization does not depend on layout algorithms. Unknown keys are prevented by TypeScript and may be detected in development diagnostics when plain JavaScript bypasses types. Every item-participation field is optional in the shared capability; the owning parent validates required fields and its accepted value subset, avoiding incompatible `alignSelf` declarations or Grid coordinates on elements outside Grid.
The first value model is deliberately small:

ts type Length = number | `${number}%` | "auto"; interface Constraints { minWidth: number; maxWidth: number; minHeight: number; maxHeight: number; } interface LayoutBox { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number; }
Grid track values add a separately parsed `fr` form. Shorthands normalize to canonical per-edge or per-axis values before an algorithm runs.
All resolved Canvas geometry is finite. Infinity may represent an internal unbounded measurement constraint but never reaches a Canvas drawing call.
Percentage resolution uses the containing layout component's content box. The first release always uses the intrinsic Canvas size as the root containing box.
The initial box model is deliberately explicit:
- `width` and `height` specify the content box, matching CSS `box-sizing: content-box`;
- layout dimensions, min/max constraints, padding, and gaps are nonnegative;
- `min > max` is invalid rather than silently reordered;
- padding is numeric only and may reduce an allocation's content box to zero, never below;
- percentages are initially accepted for sizes, offsets, and tracks, not padding or gaps;
- margin is deferred;
- signed Canvas geometry remains valid outside a layout context, but a negative dimension cannot participate as a layout allocation.
The component type remains a callable function, matching CRC's current identity and render model. Optional normalization and measurement capabilities are static metadata on that same function object:

ts type CompType = (( props: ProgramProps

, style: Readonly, ctx: RenderingContext2D, ) => CRCNode) & Readonly<{ normalizeStyle?: (style: Readonly) => Readonly; resolveStyle?: ( style: Readonly, context: StyleResolutionContext, ) => Readonly; measure?: (input: MeasureInput, N>) => MeasureResult; }>; declare function defineComp< P, S extends SystemStyle = SystemStyle, N = S, R = N, >( render: CompType, capabilities?: { normalizeStyle?: (style: Readonly) => Readonly; resolveStyle?: ( style: Readonly, context: StyleResolutionContext, ) => Readonly; measure?: (input: MeasureInput, N>) => MeasureResult; }, ): CompFactory, S>;

Capabilities are installed as non-enumerable metadata on the render function, not on each element. This preserves the function object used by CRC identity. Numeric-only styles use identity normalization and resolution. Allocation-aware styles are normalized, then resolved to finite render values before the component callback is invoked.

Drawing components render. Measurable components additionally provide a pure measurement function. Dedicated layout components provide a layout algorithm and a compatible measurement function so they can be nested inside other layouts.

Measurement cannot use CRC hooks, paint, mutate runtime ownership, or register interaction. It can use an explicitly supplied Canvas measurement service. This keeps measurement deterministic and safe to repeat or cache.
Every dedicated layout component delegates to a small algorithm module with no Canvas painting responsibility:

ts interface LayoutAlgorithm<S> { layout(input: LayoutInput<S>): LayoutResult; measure?(input: LayoutMeasureInput<S>): Size; } interface LayoutResult { container: LayoutBox; children: readonly ChildPlacement[]; } interface ChildPlacement { element: CompEl<any, any>; box: LayoutBox; clipInChildSpace?: LayoutBox; identityHint: InternalIdentityHint; }
Initial modules are isolated by semantics:
- absolute containing-box resolution;
- CRC-native flow;
- CSS-compatible flex subset;
- CSS-compatible grid subset;
- CRC-native overlay.
Algorithms depend on normalized style, constraints, and a measurement callback. They do not depend on global render state, DOM nodes, mouse events, or the Canvas drawing API.
For a drawing element, the runtime:
1. Reads its specified style.
2. Normalizes component defaults and syntax.
3. Resolves percentages and allocation-dependent values from the current layout context.
4. Invokes the component with programmatic props, resolved style, and Canvas context.
5. Traverses any non-layout children using existing parent-first semantics.

Built-in drawing primitives remain leaves. Custom components may paint and return ordinary children under CRC's existing traversal model, but only dedicated layout elements establish a formatting context.
For a dedicated layout element, its component function:
1. Receives its allocated box from the parent layout context or root Canvas.
2. Reads direct child descriptors without invoking child component functions.
3. Normalizes the container and child item styles needed by its algorithm.
4. Resolves definite sizes and calls measurement only for unresolved intrinsic inputs.
5. Produces finite child placements.
6. Returns stable internal placement elements in required paint order.
The layout component itself does not paint. Each internal placement element:
1. Saves Canvas/runtime layout state.
2. Applies the placement translation using the existing transform seam.
3. Applies CRC-managed overflow clipping when required.
4. Publishes the child's allocated local `LayoutBox` to style resolution.
5. Renders the original child element.
6. Restores state after the subtree.
This preserves one ordinary component traversal. Layout adds arrangement work but not a speculative paint pass.
A nested layout element is an ordinary item to its parent and a formatting context for its own direct children. The component name makes that role explicit:
text flex ├── rect └── grid ├── text └── image

The flex algorithm resolves the grid's outer allocation. When intrinsic size is required, it calls the grid component's pure measure capability over the grid's already-declared direct child elements. Once placed, the grid algorithm resolves its own children during normal traversal.

If an arbitrary custom component hides a future layout subtree behind its render function, its parent cannot inspect that hidden subtree. The custom component must accept a definite allocation or provide its own measurement capability.

A layout parent owns the child's allocation origin and available size. Placement translates the child's local coordinate system to that origin. Primitive `x` and `y` styles remain local geometry inside that allocation.
- At the root, the local origin is the Canvas origin.
- In `absolute`, declared positions determine placement inside the containing box.
- In flow/flex/grid/overlay, the algorithm determines placement; local primitive geometry starts at zero unless the primitive style explicitly offsets it.
- A resolved percentage width controls both the primitive's allocated width and, for box-shaped built-ins, its painted local width.
- Paint may overflow the allocation when overflow is visible. Paint bounds do not retroactively alter allocation.
Layout placement is applied before the child's own transform style. This creates the composition:
text ancestor transform × layout placement × child transform × local geometry
Interaction regions and layers capture that same composed transform. Pixel-grid adjustment runs in the component's local paint space after its resolved dimensions are known.

Visible overflow creates no layout clip. Clipped overflow adds a CRC-managed content-box clip so painting and hit testing use the same intersection. Scrolling is not implied and remains outside this architecture.

Internal placement uses one stable, module-level component type. It does not allocate a new component function per child or render. Each wrapper carries a private identity hint derived from the original child type, canonical key, and same-type occurrence. The renderer uses that hint for the wrapper's identity and then renders the original child beneath it. This preserves current unkeyed `A/B/A` behavior when `B` is inserted or removed; copying only a public key would not.
- A keyed child retains identity across reflow and supported in-parent reorder.
- Unkeyed same-type identity remains occurrence based.
- Moving an element between layout parents changes its parent path and may remount it.
- Source order remains paint and reverse target-selection order by default.
- CSS ordering features are not enabled until their paint/interaction order is implemented and documented together.
The placement wrapper is an implementation detail and does not become a public component or an extra author-visible node.
`measure` receives:
- component programmatic props;
- normalized specified style;
- finite or internally unbounded constraints;
- a Canvas text/image measurement service;
- a recursive child-measure callback for dedicated layout components.
It returns a finite preferred size before min/max clamping by the owning algorithm, or a typed unsupported-measurement result that becomes an actionable diagnostic when the size is required.

Text measurement and rendering share tokenization, line-breaking, and typography utilities so measured and painted line boxes cannot drift. Image measurement initially accepts explicit dimensions only. Natural image measurement is unsupported until resource loading has an owner that can begin outside render without violating measurement purity. Ordinary non-layout image rendering retains its current load, stale-completion, and teardown behavior.

`crcLayoutBox()` exposes the current allocation in child-local coordinates as `{ x: 0, y: 0, width, height }`. It is observational, does not schedule a render, and deliberately does not claim to provide DOM/root coordinates; callers needing those must combine it with their own transform observation.

Caching is not required initially. If structural counters demonstrate repeated identical measurement, cache keys include component type, relevant props, normalized style, constraints, and measurement-environment inputs such as font.
Reusable styles are ordinary immutable TypeScript values:

ts const cardBase = { minWidth: 240, minHeight: 120 } satisfies BoxStyle; MetricCard({ value, style: { ...cardBase, width: compact ? 280 : "100%", custom: { density: compact ? "compact" : "comfortable" }, }, });

CRC does not merge parent styles into children. A component that wants to reuse or forward style data does so explicitly in its component function. `custom` is typed by the component and ignored by system normalization.
Errors are classified close to their owner:
- style syntax/unknown value;
- non-finite resolved geometry;
- unsupported intrinsic measurement;
- cyclic or underdetermined percentage sizing;
- incompatible algorithm value;
- internal algorithm invariant violation.
Diagnostic messages include the component type, key when present, property, value, algorithm, and constraints. Production behavior never sends invalid geometry to Canvas.

A thrown layout/style error uses the existing render failure path: owned resources are released and component refs are cleared. Global Canvas and CRC state are restored in `finally` blocks. Pixels already painted earlier in the failing frame retain the existing no-rollback behavior.
The implementation should preserve these conceptual modules even if filenames differ:

text style/ types public capability interfaces normalize defaults, shorthand expansion, value parsing resolve-length number/percent/auto resolution diagnostics typed style/layout errors layout/ types constraints, sizes, boxes, placements context current allocation and containing box measure measurement dispatch and services place-child internal transform/clip placement component absolute absolute algorithm flow CRC-native flow algorithm flex CSS-compatible flex subset grid CSS-compatible grid subset overlay CRC-native overlay algorithm

Built-in drawing components depend on style normalization and current layout context. Pure layout algorithms do not depend on built-in drawing components. Render integration depends on both but remains small.
The architecture is intentionally separable:
1. Add the element/style protocol and migrate existing primitives without adding new layout behavior.
2. Add box/constraint/length resolution and root allocation.
3. Add stable placement/context integration and absolute/overlay algorithms.
4. Add pure measurement capability and migrate text/image measurement utilities.
5. Add flow, flex, and grid as isolated algorithms with focused fixtures.
6. Add package, Studio, documentation, and holistic trust closure.

At each seam, existing public rendering is either unchanged or the new behavior is exercisable through a focused public scenario. No step needs the entire layout family to exist before it can be reviewed.
Fast feedback is the default:
- Pure style/layout modules use fast non-browser unit fixtures.
- Each render-integration seam has a small focused browser contract.
- Component migrations run their existing focused tests rather than the entire repository gate after every file.
- One representative nested scenario carries geometry, pixels, hit targets, reflow, and cleanup through successive milestones.
Broader checks run after cohesive milestones:
- after all built-in components use style;
- after layout placement and measurement integrate with the runtime;
- after flex/grid reach their declared support matrices;
- once at final Plan 003 completion through the aggregate trust gate.
This cadence does not weaken correctness criteria. It avoids repeatedly paying the complete package/browser/visual cost while a local slice is still changing.
1. Declared layout boxes, not inferred paint commands, are spatial truth.
2. No retained display list is introduced for layout.
3. Style is first-class element metadata and the sole visual property namespace.
4. Cascade and inheritance do not exist.
5. CSS names imply compatible accepted behavior; divergent algorithms get new names.
6. Formatting contexts are dedicated components, never hidden on drawing primitives.
7. Direct nesting is supported without public layout-item wrappers.
8. Measurement is opt-in, pure, and separate from render hooks and ownership.
9. Placement composes through existing transforms/clips so drawing and interaction share geometry.
10. Rapid focused checks precede milestone and final holistic verification.

currentUnits.text: Status: current architecture. Project Plan 003 established style/layout on 2026-08-18; the JSX authoring pivot updated the element boundary on 2026-09-03.

This document describes how branded elements, local style, pure measurement, and declared-box layout preserve CRC's scheduled immediate-mode Canvas model. The completed Plan 003 design and implementation documents remain dated historical evidence for the original style/layout delivery; this document is the current authoring and runtime architecture.
CRC preserves:
- one live mount per Canvas and identity-guarded, idempotent disposal;
- animation-frame update coalescing and one full synchronous traversal;
- parent scope, component function, key, and occurrence identity;
- Canvas save/restore and fail-closed runtime-state restoration;
- source paint order and reverse source coordinate targeting;
- shared transform/clip/layout geometry for paint and interaction;
- globally ordered offscreen layers; and
- one explicit owner and exact teardown for every resource.
There is no DOM renderer, virtual DOM reconciliation, retained display list, style cascade, or speculative child render.
JSX and `createElement(type, props, ...children)` create the same lightweight descriptor:

ts interface CRCElement

{ readonly type: CRCElementType

; readonly props: Readonly

; readonly key?: string; } type CRCComponent

= (props: P) => CRCNode | void;

The public interface is nominally branded; the runtime uses the non-enumerable stable global symbol `Symbol.for("@crc/core.element")`. Author props are copied, `key` is removed and normalized from string/number to string, and compiler or variadic children are installed in props. Development construction shallow-freezes the synthetic props and descriptor and `jsxDEV` stores source metadata privately. Nested author objects are not deep-frozen.

The descriptor is an ephemeral description, not a retained render node. Calling a component directly does not construct one. Platform component values report a targeted error when invoked outside the renderer.
ts type CRCNode = | CRCElement<any> | false | true | null | undefined | "" | 0 | readonly CRCNode[] | Iterable<CRCNode>;

Arrays and finite synchronous iterables flatten recursively. Empty values do not create identity slots. Unkeyed fragments are transparent; keyed fragments remain one parent identity boundary. The receiving renderer, container, or layout component materializes a finite iterable once for its operation.

Raw non-empty text/numbers, Promises, async iterables, functions, symbols, foreign elements, and unsupported objects reject contextually. `Text` uses a separate scalar algebra that concatenates strings/numbers (including zero) and empty values while rejecting elements and async/unsupported input.
The runtime stores private metadata keyed by component function:
- no primitive metadata → invoke the plain function with its props;
- primitive metadata → normalize/resolve style and invoke the primitive render callback with program props, finite style, and isolated Canvas context;
- policy metadata → prepare exactly one child before identity dispatch without invoking the policy as an ordinary component.

Ordinary application components are plain functions. Simple custom painters use `useCanvasContext()` during live rendering. `definePrimitive` is reserved for platform extension requiring style stages or pure measurement:
ts const PlatformValue = definePrimitive< ProgramProps, Specified, Normalized, Resolved >(render, { normalizeStyle, resolveStyle, measure });

The returned value is an element type, not an element. Program props cannot declare reserved `key` or `style`. A specified style with allocation syntax requires a resolver and its resolved type cannot retain percentages or `"auto"`.
Transparent `FocusManagement` and `KeyboardNavigation` values attach private lifecycle descriptors to their one prepared child. They do not paint, lay out, own hooks, or add identity.
Visual and layout inputs are always inside `props.style` on the descriptor. Component-specific schemas positively opt into `SystemStyle` and remain closed. There is no inheritance stage.
1. **Specified style** is the exact author input.
2. **Normalized style** adds pure defaults and canonical syntax without parent geometry.
3. **Resolved style** applies allocation, percentage basis, and constraints and contains finite render values.

Opaque string/resource fields such as paint, font, image source, and enum values are registered so allocation-syntax diagnostics do not reinterpret them. Unknown keys are type errors and can be development diagnostics for untyped JavaScript.
Plain components continue to receive their exact specified style. A parent may inspect it for allocation, but the finite child-local allocation is exposed separately through `useLayoutBox()`.

Style schemas are capability intersections, not a global property bag. `BoxStyle`, `LayoutItemStyle`, paint/cursor types, and component-specific geometry combine only where a component supports them. Every system style positively extends `SystemStyle`; that base contains optional `custom` and no index signature. Excess keys therefore remain errors instead of silently becoming Canvas state.

This is a positive schema contract, not a blacklist: unrelated arrays, functions, dates, URLs, errors, blobs, buffers, matrices, and arbitrary resource/class types fail structurally unless their declared type deliberately opts in. Every shared item-participation field is optional; its owning parent validates required coordinates and the accepted value subset, avoiding an incompatible `alignSelf` or Grid coordinate on an element outside that layout.

`PrimitiveProgramProps

` rejects a program-prop declaration containing the reserved `key` or `style` names. `PrimitiveInput` adds `style` back as element input: the property is optional only when all members of `S` are optional. This logic distributes over unions so one invalid program-prop member or one required style member cannot hide behind another union arm.

The descriptor keeps one `props` object, including specified `style` and `children`. Separation happens only at primitive dispatch: the render callback receives reserved metadata apart from its ordinary program props. Plain functions receive their author props normally.
The common allocation vocabulary remains deliberately finite:

ts type Percentage = `${number}%`; type Length = number | Percentage | "auto"; interface Constraints { minWidth: number; maxWidth: number; minHeight: number; maxHeight: number; } interface LayoutBox { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number; }

Infinity may represent an internal unbounded measurement constraint but never reaches Canvas drawing. Layout sizes, min/max constraints, padding, and gaps are nonnegative; `min > max` is invalid. `width` and `height` describe the content box. Numeric padding may shrink a content allocation to zero, not below zero. Percentages resolve against the containing component's content box. `Grid` tracks add their separately parsed fractional form. Shorthands normalize to canonical per-edge or per-axis values before an algorithm runs. Percentages are accepted for documented sizes, offsets, and tracks, not padding or gaps. Signed Canvas geometry can remain valid outside layout, but a negative dimension cannot participate as a layout allocation.

The root allocation follows the [Canvas surface contract](../design/canvas-surface-contract.md): a fixed logical viewport is captured at mount by default, while responsive mode follows the CSS content box. Surface projection and backing density do not leak into local layout units.
Margin, scrolling, implicit Grid placement, reverse/reordered Flexbox, and advanced intrinsic CSS sizing stay outside this architecture.

Each dedicated layout component delegates placement to an isolated algorithm with no Canvas-paint responsibility. Conceptually it consumes normalized container/item style, constraints, and a measurement callback, then produces a finite container box and ordered child placements. The five algorithms are separate by semantics:

ts interface LayoutResult { container: LayoutBox; children: readonly ChildPlacement[]; } interface ChildPlacement { element: CRCElement; box: LayoutBox; clipInChildSpace?: LayoutBox; identityHint: InternalIdentityHint; }
- `Absolute`: independent offsets within a containing box;
- `Overlay`: one shared allocation plus alignment;
- `Flow`: CRC-native sequential placement and optional wrapping;
- `Flex`: the documented CSS-compatible subset; and
- `Grid`: explicit fixed/percentage/fractional tracks and explicit placement.

Algorithms do not depend on global render state, DOM nodes, user events, or Canvas drawing calls. CSS-named values are accepted only where CRC implements their documented behavior; divergent algorithms retain CRC-specific names.
For a platform drawing/composition element the runtime:
1. reads specified style from `element.props.style`;
2. applies the component's pure normalizer;
3. resolves allocation-dependent values from the current layout context;
4. validates that render geometry is finite;
5. invokes the primitive callback with program props, resolved style, and the isolated Canvas context; and
6. traverses any declared container children in source order.
Drawing leaves do not establish formatting contexts. `Group`, `Clip`, and `Layer` compose recursive children but are not layout algorithms.
For a dedicated layout element the runtime:
1. receives its allocated box from its parent or root;
2. prepares direct branded child descriptors without invoking their component functions;
3. normalizes only the container/item style required by the algorithm;
4. resolves definite inputs and requests pure measurement only for unresolved used sizes;
5. calculates finite ordered placements; and
6. traverses stable private placement descriptors in paint order.

A placement descriptor saves Canvas/runtime layout state, translates to the child allocation, applies CRC-owned overflow clipping, publishes a child-local `LayoutBox`, traverses the author element, and restores state. This remains one normal render traversal, never a speculative paint pass.
A nested layout component is one item to its parent and a formatting context for its own direct children:
text Flex ├── Rectangle └── Grid ├── Text └── Image

The outer algorithm resolves the inner layout's allocation. When an intrinsic size is required, it asks the inner platform value's pure measurement capability about its already-declared children. Normal traversal later performs the actual inner layout and paint. A plain component that hides a layout subtree is opaque to its parent and therefore needs a definite outer size.

Each layout component prepares one immutable direct-element array before algorithm work. It normalizes direct child style without invoking child functions. Flow/Flex/Grid call pure measurement only when a used size is not definite.
For each result, CRC creates a branded private placement clone that preserves the author descriptor and records per-occurrence used style/identity metadata in weak storage. Placement then:
1. saves Canvas and runtime layout state;
2. translates to the child's border/content allocation;
3. applies overflow clipping when requested;
4. publishes the child-local `LayoutBox`;
5. traverses the original child component; and
6. restores state after its subtree.

Nested layout is ordinary composition. The outer algorithm sizes the inner layout value; the inner value establishes a formatting context for its own prepared direct children during normal traversal. A plain component exposes no intrinsic measurement capability and therefore needs a definite allocation when it hides that subtree from its parent. Custom platform normalization, resolution, or pure measurement requires a value made with `definePrimitive`; those capabilities never attach to an ordinary plain component.

Private placement metadata includes the original child type, canonical key, and same-type occurrence. One stable module-level placement component is reused instead of allocating a new function per child or render. A keyed child survives supported same-parent reflow; unkeyed `A/B/A` identity still follows the two occurrences of `A`; moving a child between parents remounts it. The placement descriptor never becomes a public wrapper or author-visible node. CSS ordering features remain disabled until allocation, paint/interaction order, and identity are implemented and documented together.

Measurement receives program props, normalized style, constraints, an explicit Canvas text service, and a recursive `measureElement`. It returns measured content size or an unsupported reason. It cannot paint, invoke hooks, `useCanvasContext`, `useLayoutBox`, create targets or layers, schedule work, or acquire runtime resources. Pure measurement cannot create image generations. Temporary globals are cleared/restored in `finally`, and cycles are diagnosed. Pure measurement isolates itself from active render hooks and layout context.

`Text` shares tokenization, line breaking, typography, and one content/layout calculation between measurement and paint in a render transaction, so measured and painted line boxes cannot drift. Explicitly sized `Image` can measure; natural image size cannot because it would acquire asynchronous state. Plain components do not claim measurement. A supported result is a finite preferred size before min/max clamping by the owning algorithm; an unsupported result becomes an actionable diagnostic when that size is required.

`useLayoutBox()` exposes `{ x: 0, y: 0, width, height }` in the allocated child-local coordinate system. It is observational and does not claim root or DOM coordinates. Measurement caching is not required; if introduced after structural evidence, a cache key must include component type, relevant props, normalized style, constraints, and environment inputs such as font metrics.

Layout owns the child's allocation origin and available size. Placement translates into child-local coordinates. Primitive `x`/`y` remain local paint offsets; parent `left`/`top` remain allocation offsets.
The complete composition equation is:
text root surface × ancestor Group × layout placement × child Group × local geometry
- At the root, local origin is the Canvas logical origin.
- `Absolute` uses declared positions within its containing box.
- `Flow`, `Flex`, `Grid`, and `Overlay` choose placement; local primitive geometry starts at zero unless the primitive style explicitly offsets it.
- A resolved percentage width controls both allocation and, for box-shaped built-ins, painted local width.
- Paint may overflow a visible allocation and never retroactively changes it.

The same composition is captured for interaction paths, explicit clips, layout-overflow clips, and `Layer` bounds. Paint may overflow a visible allocation without changing allocation. Layers mount a stable private fragment root in their offscreen instance and join the root paint ledger at their composite position.
Layout placement applies before a child's own transform. Pixel-grid adjustment runs in the component's local paint space after resolved dimensions are known.
Visible overflow creates no layout clip. Clipped overflow adds a CRC-managed content-box clip whose intersection is shared by paint and hit testing; it does not imply scrolling.
Reusable styles remain ordinary immutable values and object composition:

tsx const cardBase = { minWidth: 240, minHeight: 120 } satisfies BoxStyle; const card = ( <MetricCard value={value} style={{ ...cardBase, width: compact ? 280 : "100%", custom: { density: compact ? "compact" : "comfortable" }, }} /> );
CRC never merges parent style into a child. A component forwards or derives the style fields it intentionally owns. System normalization ignores application-owned `custom` data.

Diagnostics are raised by the closest responsible boundary: invalid style syntax or unknown value, non-finite resolution, unsupported/cyclic or underdetermined percentage measurement, incompatible algorithm input, or an internal algorithm invariant. A `LayoutDiagnostic` records component, key when present, property, supplied value, algorithm, constraints, and reason. Invalid geometry never reaches Canvas.

A layout/style throw enters the ordinary render-failure path. Runtime-owned resources and refs close, Canvas and temporary state restore in `finally`, and the next explicit root can mount cleanly. Pixels already painted earlier in the failed frame retain the renderer's documented no-rollback behavior.

Render setup records the current element, component refs, hook index, layout box, primitive receiver, context, clip stack, and seen identities. All are restored in `finally`. A throw closes runtime-owned refs/resources rather than retaining a partial tree; earlier frame pixels are not transactional.

Successful traversal removes unseen identities only after the tree completes. Every hook cleanup, event registration, image generation, layer instance, surface observer, and pending frame has one owner. Private weak metadata does not become a lifetime owner.
The implementation keeps these conceptual seams even when helper filenames differ:

text element/ types, creation, child materialization, fragments, private metadata style/ types public capability interfaces normalize defaults, shorthand expansion, value parsing resolve-length number/percentage/auto resolution diagnostics typed style/layout errors layout/ types constraints, sizes, boxes, placements context current allocation and containing box measure measurement dispatch and services place-child private transform/clip placement component absolute, overlay, flow, flex, grid focus/ transparent policy metadata and the root focus manager

Built-in primitives depend on style resolution and current allocation. Pure layout algorithms do not depend on drawing primitives. Runtime dispatch is the small integration seam that understands element, primitive, layout, and policy metadata.

baselineUnits.text: CRC logical focus is not screen-reader semantics. Adding `withFocusManagement` makes explicit Canvas targets operable through a shared keyboard focus host; it does not give those targets DOM roles, accessible names, states, relationships, text selection, or screen-reader announcements. It does not make a Canvas application accessible by itself.

When meaningful information or operations exist only in Canvas pixels, the application must provide an equivalent semantic experience. Use the application framework or DOM strategy already appropriate to the product. CRC does not require a framework and does not prescribe a persistent DOM descendant for every drawn target.
The application-owned experience should expose:
- meaningful names, roles, descriptions, states, values, and relationships;
- the same important data conveyed visually, not only a prose description of the drawing;
- equivalent operations for every meaningful Canvas action;
- native editable controls and text selection where editing is part of the task;
- announcements or status updates when users need them to understand change;
- an accessible name and concise usage instructions for the Canvas whenever it remains a keyboard interaction surface.

Canvas fallback content may be a useful host for the alternative DOM. A nearby or mode-switched semantic view can also be appropriate. The right structure depends on the application's information and workflow, not on CRC internals.

Treat the Canvas and semantic alternative as two presentations of the same application model. Names, values, selected state, disabled state, ordering, validation, results, and available operations must stay synchronized in both directions. A change made through the Canvas should be observable through the alternative, and an equivalent DOM action should update the Canvas.

Do not infer semantic state from pixels after painting. Keep that state in the application model and render both experiences from it. Likewise, do not use CRC's opaque logical target object as a semantic identifier; use stable application-owned IDs and labels.

A Canvas focus host and a simultaneously tabbable semantic alternative can create duplicate or invisible keyboard stops for the same operation. Decide which surface participates in the active keyboard experience and make the other representation noncompeting or clearly distinct. Do not leave hidden interactive controls in the Tab order, and do not require users to traverse the same logical operation twice.

This does not mean that only one representation may exist. A visual Canvas and a semantic DOM view may coexist when their purpose and focus behavior are clear. The application owns entry, exit, focus restoration, view switching, and announcements across those surfaces; CRC does not silently merge application DOM into its logical focus index.

This document defines how a root CRC mount maps logical drawing units to the Canvas CSS content box and physical backing store. The mapping is owned by the runtime so drawing, layout, interaction, clipping, and offscreen layers use one coordinate model.
`crc(canvas, element, config?)` accepts one mount-time surface configuration:

ts type CRCFit = "contain" | "cover" | "fill" | "none" | "scale-down"; type CRCPixelRatio = "device" | number; type CRCConfig = | { signal?: AbortSignal; viewport?: Readonly<{ width: number; height: number }>; fit?: CRCFit; pixelRatio?: CRCPixelRatio; } | { signal?: AbortSignal; viewport: "responsive"; pixelRatio?: CRCPixelRatio; };

The configuration belongs to the first live mount. Later `crc()` calls update the root element but do not replace the surface configuration or mount signal. Dispose and remount to select a different surface mode.
The defaults are:
- a fixed logical viewport captured from the Canvas `width` and `height` attributes at mount time;
- centered `contain` fitting into the current CSS content box; and
- the live `window.devicePixelRatio`.

An explicit fixed `viewport` decouples logical scene size from the initial backing attributes. `viewport: 'responsive'` instead makes the current CSS content-box width and height the logical root allocation. Responsive mode does not accept `fit`, because its logical and display extents are identical.
`pixelRatio` may be `'device'` or any finite number greater than zero. The default `'device'` mode observes density changes. A numeric value is stable and does not acquire device-density listeners.
Invalid viewports, pixel ratios, and fit values throw synchronously on mount. A root mount also requires `ResizeObserver`.
CRC distinguishes:
1. **logical space**, used by components, styles, layout boxes, paths, and `CRCMouseEvent.x/y`;
2. **display space**, measured from the Canvas CSS content box in CSS pixels;
3. **backing space**, stored by `canvas.width` and `canvas.height` in physical pixels.
The backing dimensions are independently rounded:
text backingWidth = max(1, round(displayWidth * pixelRatio)) backingHeight = max(1, round(displayHeight * pixelRatio))

CRC derives the effective backing density from those rounded dimensions and installs one root transform before rendering. Component-local transforms then compose after that root transform. The bitmap is cleared in backing space before the root transform is installed.

CSS borders and padding are excluded when measuring display space. If changing backing attributes would otherwise feed intrinsic Canvas dimensions back into CSS sizing, CRC temporarily owns an equivalent inline CSS width and/or height to stabilize the original content box. Disposal restores only inline values still owned by that mount and never overwrites a later external change.
Fixed fitting is centered on both axes:
| Fit | Scale behavior |
| `contain` | Uniformly scale until the whole logical viewport fits; unused display space remains around it. |
| `cover` | Uniformly scale until the display is covered; logical edges may be outside the display. |
| `fill` | Scale each axis independently to fill the display exactly. |
| `none` | Preserve one logical unit per CSS pixel and center the viewport without scaling. |
| `scale-down` | Use `none` when the viewport fits; otherwise use `contain`. |
Centering offsets may be fractional. CRC does not currently expose alignment or background/letterbox paint options. Content outside the Canvas bitmap is naturally clipped by the platform.

For `viewport: 'responsive'`, one logical unit equals one CSS content-box pixel. A CSS resize updates the root `crcLayoutBox()` allocation and schedules one coalesced frame without remounting component identity. Backing dimensions still follow the requested pixel ratio, so responsive layout and high-density paint remain independent concerns.
A zero-sized display axis temporarily suppresses rendering rather than inventing a logical size or one-pixel layout. A later positive resize resumes the same live mount.

Native mouse positions are first measured relative to the Canvas content box, then mapped through backing space and the inverse root render transform. The public event therefore reports logical coordinates for every fit and density. Letterboxed points can be outside the fixed logical viewport; only registered logical paths that actually contain the mapped point can become targets.

Every captured interaction transform and clip omits the already-applied root surface transform. Hit testing maps the native point back to logical space and installs each captured logical transform on its isolated test context, so paint and targeting do not double-apply density or fit.

Managed `layer` backing stores inherit the root's current backing pixels per logical unit on both axes. A density or projection change rerenders a layer at the new physical size and composites its complete backing source into its logical destination. Layer-local layout and interaction remain expressed in logical units.

Resize and density notifications use the ordinary animation-frame scheduler. Multiple notifications while a frame is pending coalesce without canceling and moving that frame later. Device-density observation uses both the current resolution media query and window resize as platform signals, rebinding after a density change.

The root surface owns its `ResizeObserver`, density listeners, resolution media query listener, and any intrinsic-size stabilization. Abort, controller disposal, and failed-mount cleanup release the exact owned resources. A stale observer or controller cannot mutate a replacement mount.

Pure projection tests cover every fit, responsive resolution, independent rounding, invalid input, default capture, layer density, and zero display size. Root lifecycle tests cover fixed and responsive resize, identity preservation, device density, intrinsic-size stabilization, and disposal. Interaction and layer suites prove logical coordinates and nested high-density composition.

The public `canvas-surface` laboratory is loaded by both the Studio and headless Chromium. It proves fixed 2x backing, fixed CSS resize without logical reflow, responsive logical reflow without remount, and logical mouse coordinates. Full-page Studio baselines provide the corresponding sharpness and composition evidence.

This document defines CRC's drawing and composition exports. Rendered values use the required local language in the [style-system contract](./style-system-contract.md); layout participation follows the [layout-system contract](./layout-system-contract.md). Events remain program props. Geometry, paint, cursor, clipping, transform, text, and image source are style. Runtime legacy aliases and top-level visual props are unsupported.
- Drawing follows Canvas 2D geometry, paint order, transforms, clipping, text measurement, image decoding, and `Path2D` parsing.
- `opacity` multiplies the current Canvas global alpha when supplied. Zero opacity paints nothing but does not remove an otherwise interactive geometry region.
- Transparent or absent visible paint does not itself remove interaction geometry. Target selection follows the region rules in the mouse contract.
- Property changes replace the prior frame's pixels and interaction geometry after the scheduled CRC render settles.
- Empty paths and zero-length lines are safe no-ops. Signed primitive rectangle and image dimensions follow Canvas geometry; layout allocation remains nonnegative.

- Pixel-grid alignment is optional. `none` preserves the exact input. `round`, `ceil`, and `floor` snap opposite rectangle edges or the line coordinate using the effective stroke offset, preserving the signed span instead of adding one pixel.
- Browser-defined values remain browser-defined: malformed SVG path data is delegated to `Path2D`; decoded image edge antialiasing and system-font glyph rasterization can vary by platform.
| Public export | Supported contract | Primary evidence |

| `rect` | Required local `width` and `height`; optional `x` and `y` default zero; fill, stroke, opacity, signed geometry, pixel-grid modes, cursor, and mouse regions. | Direct component suite, shapes lesson, geometry matrix |
| `path` | Required `Path2D` `d`; fill, stroke, opacity, path replacement, expanded stroke interaction width, and empty paths. | Direct component and interaction suites, shapes lesson |
| `line` | Ordered polyline coordinates, style/update behavior, empty and one-point no-op geometry, transforms/clips, and expanded hit width. | Direct line suite, lines lesson, geometry matrix |
| `horizontalLine` | Required local `y`; optional `x1` default zero and `x2` default allocation width; pixel-grid modes and shared line paint/interaction. | Direct helper matrix and lines lesson |
| `verticalLine` | Required local `x`; optional `y1` default zero and `y2` default allocation height; pixel-grid modes and parity with `horizontalLine`. | Direct helper matrix and lines lesson |

| `svgPath` | Required string `d`; browser `Path2D` parsing, fill/stroke/opacity, data updates, interactions, empty/malformed delegation, and transforms. | Direct SVG suite, shapes lesson, runtime recovery suite |

| `text` | Required text; local position, font, alignment and baseline; `visible`, `ellipsis`, `squish`, and `clip` fit modes; wrapping box; paint/opacity/cursor; measured per-line interaction bounds and pure measurement. | Direct call/interaction suite and text lesson |

| `img` | Required `src`; detachable source generations; success/error/race/removal; natural or explicit dimensions; border stroke, opacity, pixel-grid modes, and stable explicit geometry before/after load. | Direct async/component suites, image lesson, cleanup laboratory |
| `g` | Nested scale, rotation/origin, translation, skew, zero/negative scale, updates, and sibling transform isolation. | Direct group suite, composition lesson, geometry matrix |

| `clip` | `nonzero` and `evenodd` fill rules, cumulative intersections, transforms, updates, empty clips, and identical render/hit clipping. | Direct clip suite, composition lesson, geometry matrix |

| `layer` | Same-mount root/prop/dimension updates, root-density backing stores, nested and transformed offscreen composition, global paint order, interaction bounds, and cascading cleanup. | Direct layer suite, composition lesson, geometry and cleanup matrices |

Root and layer paint use logical units defined by the [Canvas surface contract](./canvas-surface-contract.md). Pixel-grid alignment therefore operates in logical geometry before the root or inherited layer density transform rasterizes it. Managed layers inherit both root backing densities and composite their complete physical source into the declared logical destination.

`text` lays out one line unless `wrap` is true. Wrapped lines accumulate without losing the final fitting line. `lineHeight` advances each line. A finite style height limits complete lines; ellipsis applies to the final visible line when requested. An ellipsis narrower than three dots resolves to an empty string.

`fit: "squish"` passes the supplied width to Canvas text paint. `fit: "clip"` creates a finite alignment- and baseline-aware clip rectangle when width is supplied; omitted height uses the Canvas allocation. Interaction paths union actual metrics for every rendered line. Paint and pure measurement share this resolver, so measured wrapping and eventual rendering agree.

Exact Canvas calls are tested with controlled text metrics. Gallery image comparison masks only glyph rasterization, while surrounding cards, clipping, layout, state, and interaction bounds remain exact.

Each `style.src` owns one `Image` generation. Load and error handlers detach on settlement, source replacement, component removal, or instance disposal. Saved late callbacks and superseded loads cannot change current state. Successful natural sizing uses `naturalWidth`/`naturalHeight` independently for omitted dimensions. Explicit dimensions establish geometry before load and after failure; this matches CRC's geometry-first transparent-region rule. Natural image size is unavailable to pure layout measurement because it would acquire an asynchronous resource.
Pixel alignment produces one adjusted rectangle used by `drawImage`, the optional border, and the interaction path. It does not stretch the image by an extra pixel.

CRC exports descriptive component values. Authors construct them with JSX or `createElement`; none is a callable factory. Geometry, paint, cursor, transform, clip, image source, and layout participation use explicit local `style`. Events remain props. Drawing leaves reject children, `Text` accepts textual children, and composition values accept recursive `CRCNode` children.
First-class filters are also explicit local style and use the composition boundary defined below.

- Canvas drawing follows Canvas 2D geometry, source paint order, transforms, clips, text measurement, image decoding, and `Path2D` parsing. External renderer internals remain application-owned and are flattened at the layer boundary.
- `opacity` multiplies current global alpha. Zero paints nothing but does not remove otherwise registered interaction geometry.

- Canvas leaves and committed render-layer targets contribute their supported geometry to hit resolution by default, even without handlers, cursor, or focus metadata. `pointerEvents="none"` removes that leaf from targeting without changing paint. Absent visible paint does not by itself remove declared geometry.
- Property changes replace the prior frame's pixels and interaction geometry after the scheduled CRC render settles.

- Empty paths, zero-length lines, zero radii, zero ellipse axes, and zero-angle sweeps are safe. Signed primitive rectangle/image geometry follows Canvas; shape radii and layout allocation remain nonnegative.

- Pixel-grid alignment is optional. `none` preserves the exact input. `round`, `ceil`, and `floor` snap opposite rectangle edges or the line coordinate using the effective stroke offset, preserving the signed span instead of adding one pixel.
- Platform-defined parsing, glyph rasterization, image decoding, CORS/taint, and antialiasing remain platform-defined.

- Filters affect pixels only. They do not change measurement, layout boxes, hit paths, focus or keyboard-navigation bounds, pointer coordinates, cursor regions, or source paint order; visual overflow outside those logical shapes is not independently interactive.

Every drawing value accepts the supported DOM-aligned event/focus props through its props type. With default `pointerEvents="auto"`, it owns a stable logical target and may occlude a registered target painted behind it even when passive. Empty/unsupported local geometry remains a miss. Handler props on `Group`, `Clip`, `Layer`, and layout containers are propagation listeners only and add no structural rectangle target.

`Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Arc`, `Wedge`, and `Polygon` are dedicated drawing leaves. They use fresh immediate `Path2D` geometry on each traversal and share the `Path` paint and event-target pipeline; they do not form a retained shape graph or cache geometry. Every shape supports `cursor`, `opacity`, `stroke`, `strokeWidth`, and `lineInteractionWidth`. `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Wedge`, and `Polygon` also support `fill`. `Arc` is deliberately stroke-only because filling its open path would introduce implicit chord geometry.

Named position and radius lengths use the primitive's existing percentage basis. `cx` and `radiusX` percentages resolve against its width, while `cy` and `radiusY` percentages resolve against its height. A circular `radius` percentage resolves against the smaller of those two dimensions. Numeric geometry is in local logical Canvas units. Missing `cx` and `cy` default to zero; ellipse `rotation` defaults to zero radians; and Arc/Wedge `counterclockwise` defaults to `false`. Percentage lengths retain the standard finite and definite-basis diagnostics, and `"auto"` is not valid shape geometry.

Circle has required `radius`. Ellipse has required `radiusX` and `radiusY`, and its optional finite `rotation` is in radians. Arc and Wedge have required `radius`, `startAngle`, and `endAngle`; their angles are finite radians and their direction and angle normalization follow `Path2D.arc`. A clockwise difference of at least `2π`, or a counterclockwise difference of at least `2π` in that requested direction, is a full turn. Opposite-direction differences wrap in the requested direction as Canvas specifies.

Arc geometry stays open and exposes only its curved stroke. A partial Wedge moves from the center to the arc start, follows the circular sweep, and closes back to the center, so both radial edges participate in stroke targeting. A full-turn Wedge instead creates closed circular geometry without center or radial segments; this prevents a visible radial stroke seam. Wedge has no `innerRadius`.

Polygon takes required `coords: [number, number][]`, connects the points in order, and closes the path. Every coordinate must be finite; a failure is a `LayoutDiagnostic` whose property path identifies the offending tuple member. Polygon coordinates remain numeric because an arbitrary tuple has no unambiguous percentage basis. Fewer than three points produce empty geometry.

All radii must resolve to finite nonnegative numbers. Negative radii and non-finite angles or ellipse rotation fail style resolution with a contextual `LayoutDiagnostic`, rather than exposing a native `Path2D` exception. A zero circle radius, either zero ellipse radius, or a zero angular span produces empty geometry and paints nothing. Empty geometry still follows normal update, replacement, failure-cleanup, removal, and disposal semantics.

Paint and coordinate targeting use the exact same generated path. Fill targets use filled shape geometry when fill interaction is active; stroke targets use the existing `strokeWidth` and `lineInteractionWidth` rules. Explicit `keyboardNavigationBounds` always wins. Otherwise Circle uses center/radius bounds, rotated Ellipse uses its axis-aligned rotated extrema, Arc uses its endpoints and swept cardinal extrema, Wedge additionally includes its center, and Polygon uses point extrema. Existing Group transforms, clips, layers, focus policies, and global paint order continue to apply.

These five leaves have no intrinsic measurement: drawing radius or coordinates do not claim a layout size. Percentage geometry resolves against parent allocation, and a layout path that needs measurement must receive a declared box. Curved and arbitrary edges also do not support pixel-grid alignment.

`Text` concatenates strings and numbers, including zero, from recursive arrays or finite synchronous iterables. Booleans and nullish values add nothing. It rejects CRC elements, Promises, async iterables, functions, symbols, foreign elements, and unsupported objects. Text content is not a style member.

`CRCTextInput` additionally accepts signals at positions in that declared recursive grammar. Each directly encountered signal is read by the receiving `Text` component and may replace one complete `CRCTextChild` structure. CRC does not perform another signal-unwrapping pass inside the structure returned by that signal. Structural `CRCNodeInput` follows the same rule for roots, containers, arrays, and finite iterables.
tsx <Text style={{ x: 40, y: 80, fill: "black" }}> Hello {name} — {0} unread </Text>

The materialized value is reused by measurement and paint in one receiving transaction. The default is one line. When `wrap` is true, wrapped lines accumulate without losing the final fitting line. `lineHeight` advances each line. A finite style height limits complete lines; ellipsis applies to the final visible line when requested. An ellipsis box narrower than three dots resolves to an empty string.

`fit: "squish"` passes the supplied width to Canvas text paint. `fit: "clip"` creates a finite alignment- and baseline-aware clip rectangle when width is supplied; omitted height uses the Canvas allocation. Interaction paths union actual metrics for every rendered line. Paint and pure measurement share this resolver, so measured wrapping and eventual rendering agree.
Exact Canvas calls are tested with controlled text metrics. Image comparison masks only glyph rasterization; surrounding cards, clipping, layout, state, and interaction bounds remain exact.
| Export | Contract |
| `Group` | Applies nested scale, rotation/origin, translation, and skew to all recursive children. Updates, zero/negative scale, and sibling isolation retain Canvas semantics. |
| `Clip` | Applies required `Path2D` `d` and optional `nonzero`/`evenodd` rule to all children. Nested intersections, transforms, updates, empty clips, and paint/hit geometry agree. |
| `Layer` | Renders multiple children into one persistent offscreen CRC instance, caches retained content, follows root density, and participates in global paint/target/focus order. |

`defineRenderLayer()` creates one Canvas composition primitive for an application-owned external renderer. `defineThreeLayer()` specializes that public lifecycle for an ordinary Three.js scene and camera. The layer resolves a finite logical box, renders one private surface, and transactionally publishes one bitmap plus matching interaction metadata at its Canvas source position.

The layer is flattened: its internal objects cannot alternate around a Canvas sibling. Parent `Group` transforms, `Clip` geometry, layout, opacity, and filters apply to the completed bitmap. Three objects are ordinary Three values, not CRC elements; CRC does not mirror their geometry, material, lighting, camera, loader, shadow, control, particle, or post-processing APIs.

Default Three raycasting distinguishes visible blocks, registered CRC targets, and empty-pixel misses. The complete lifecycle, event/focus arbitration, input bridge, ownership, and deliberate boundaries are defined by the [external render-layer and Three.js contract](./render-layer-and-three-contract.md).

A nonempty `style.filter` turns the receiving primitive into one immediate-mode composition boundary. CRC renders that primitive and every descendant it returns once into one upright local source surface, then applies the complete filter list in one native Canvas operation. Fill and stroke, multiline text, transparent image content and borders, custom primitive paint, layout output, and overlapping descendants therefore contribute one combined alpha silhouette. In particular, `dropShadow` derives one shadow from that combined silhouette rather than one shadow per draw or child.

List functions consume the preceding result in declaration order. Nested filtered primitives are separate boundaries and resolve inside out: the inner filtered result becomes ordinary source paint for its parent before the parent filter runs. Component functions and primitive callbacks still execute once; filters add bitmap composition, not a second tree traversal or retained drawing commands.

Runtime-owned layout placement and the receiving `Group` transform are applied after the receiving filter. The subtree is filtered upright in local coordinates, then scaled, rotated, translated, or skewed at composite time, so a circular local blur may become elliptical under nonuniform scale and a local shadow offset rotates with its Group. An unfiltered descendant Group is already transformed inside an ancestor's source; a descendant Group with its own filter filters in its own local space before its transform reaches the ancestor source.
The receiving `Clip` also applies after its receiving filter. Descendant clips are captured inside the source, while ancestor clips constrain the completed filtered result. The composition order is:
text local subtree paint -> receiving filter -> receiving clip -> receiving transform -> ancestor clip/alpha/compositing -> parent target

`Layer` remains the persistent cache boundary; filter scratch surfaces are transient and do not create nested CRC mounts. A filter on a Layer consumes its combined cached bitmap. Changing only an outer or Layer filter can recomposite that bitmap without rerunning retained child components. Filters inside a Layer belong to the child CRC instance and its scratch pool, while the existing bridge keeps their interaction entries in global paint order.

An external render layer is another persistent cache boundary. A receiving core filter consumes its whole committed bitmap before outer clip/transform/presentation. Filter pixels do not alter the layer's committed pick or focus geometry.

Nonempty filters require browser `OffscreenCanvas`, an Offscreen Canvas 2D context, and its native `filter` state to accept the compiled chain. CRC has no DOM-canvas fallback, JavaScript pixel loop, tiling, or silent resolution reduction. An empty list stays on the direct path and has no such requirement.

`Layer` uses children, not a render element/descriptor prop. It installs a stable private keyed fragment as the offscreen root. Direct child iterables are materialized once; retained comparisons do not consume opaque nested iterables. Cache hits replay focus metadata without executing child components. Removal recursively disposes its controller, targets, frames, images, and nested layers.

On one persistent mount, a `Layer` invalidates and rerenders when its retained child root type/key, child props (including enumerable symbol keys), specified style, direct-child sequence, or layer dimensions change. Same-mount root, prop, and dimension updates replace the prior offscreen content; an unchanged retained tree reuses the cached backing store. Root density changes independently resize and rerender that backing store.

Managed layers require `OffscreenCanvas`. Their backing stores inherit both root densities and composite the complete physical source into the declared logical destination. Transforms, clips, layout overflow, events, and focus use the same geometry as paint.

Each `style.src` creates a source-tagged image generation. Load/error handlers detach on settlement, source replacement, component removal, or disposal. Saved late callbacks cannot publish stale state. Successful natural sizing uses `naturalWidth` and `naturalHeight` independently for whichever dimension is omitted. Explicit dimensions establish geometry before load and after failure; this matches CRC's geometry-first transparent-region rule. Natural image size is unavailable to pure measurement because it would acquire an asynchronous resource.
Pixel alignment produces one adjusted rectangle used by `drawImage`, the optional border, and the interaction path. It does not stretch the image by an extra pixel.

The Studio exposes one lesson for each drawing/composition value under `#/examples/drawing/rectangle` through `#/examples/drawing/image`, including the five standard-shape lessons, and `#/examples/composition/group` through `#/examples/composition/layer`. It also retains the five stable `#/testing/drawing-*` integration fixtures. Their `.example.tsx` modules are loaded by both Studio and browser tests. The stable 480×240 baselines retain semantic, Canvas-call, geometry, interaction, and inspected-pixel evidence. Image comparison masks only glyph rasterization and decoded-SVG edges where documented; surrounding cards, clipping, layout, state, and interaction bounds remain exact.

The Studio additionally exposes `#/examples/composition/filters` and the deterministic `#/testing/filters` laboratory. Filter evidence covers every function, ordered lists, inside-out nesting, combined silhouettes, Group/Clip/Layer order, local transforms and density, custom paint, edge expansion, unchanged interaction geometry, pool ownership/failure cleanup, and structural cost. Its image comparison masks only browser-sensitive filter regions where documented.

The Studio's `#/examples/three/three-layer` lesson covers blocking geometry, registered CRC targets, empty-pixel pass-through, focus, and outer Canvas filters. `#/examples/three/three-instancing` adapts Three's instancing/raycasting example and additionally covers direct Three imports, controls input, scheduled animation, camera updates, and deterministic resource ownership.

CRC adds no rich text, semantic DOM, accessibility tree, image CORS policy, SVG validator, retained scene graph, generic `Shape` component or registry, or complete CSS formatting engine. The standard shapes add no line smoothing, spline selection, data-to-mark conversion, `Pie`, charts, scales, axes, legends, annular wedges, new paint effects, or intrinsic geometry measurement. See the [style](./style-system-contract.md), [layout](./layout-system-contract.md), and [runtime](./runtime-hooks-contract.md) contracts.
The filter surface does not accept raw CSS strings, `url()`/SVG graphs, backdrop sampling, or a box-shadow model.

CRC adds no 3D scene graph, material, lighting, shadow, loader, controls, particle, or post-processing vocabulary. An external render layer remains one flattened Canvas entry; applications use Three objects and facilities directly inside `defineThreeLayer()` when they need them.

Omitting both properties keeps the existing sharp path. `cornerRadii` cannot be longer than the actual corner count, even when the extra entries are nullish. Component percentage radii resolve against the smaller dimension of that shape's current percentage basis; creator radii are finite numeric logical Canvas units only.

currentUnits.section: Rounded shapes and public path creators
currentUnits.text: Corner indices are directed: Rectangle uses `(x, y)`, `(x + width, y)`, `(x + width, y + height)`, and `(x, y + height)`; Polygon uses `coords` order; RegularPolygon uses generated vertex order; and Star uses generated traversal order, where even indices are outer tips and odd indices are inner valleys. `Rectangle` first applies its existing pixel-grid adjustment, then delegates the effective signed box and expanded radii to Canvas `roundRect`. Canvas owns signed-box physical-corner remapping and native radius scaling. Rounded closed polygons instead apply one global scale factor to all requested nonzero radii when adjacent tangent demands exceed an edge, preserving their proportions; duplicate or exactly collinear vertices remain sharp. Rounding never expands a rectangle box or coordinate/vertex extrema.

currentUnits.section: Rounded shapes and public path creators
currentUnits.text: `RegularPolygon` requires an integer `sides >= 3` and exactly one size field. For `n = sides`, CRC normalizes `circumradius`, `inradius`, or `sideLength` to the circumradius `R` as `R = circumradius`, `R = inradius / Math.cos(Math.PI / n)`, or `R = sideLength / (2 * Math.sin(Math.PI / n))`. Its finite `rotation` defaults to `-Math.PI / 2`; increasing angles generate vertices clockwise in Canvas coordinates. `Star` requires an integer `points >= 3`, finite nonnegative `outerRadius` and `innerRadius`, and `innerRadius <= outerRadius`. `points` counts outer tips. With the same default rotation, Star emits clockwise, alternating outer/even and inner/odd vertices. It is one concave silhouette: a six-point star has twelve alternating corners, not two crossing triangles.

currentUnits.section: Rounded shapes and public path creators
currentUnits.text: All components use the canonical creator-generated path for paint, stroke, events, clipping intersections, transforms, layers, and focus. Explicit `keyboardNavigationBounds` wins. Otherwise rounded Rectangle uses its resolved box, rounded Polygon uses coordinate extrema, and RegularPolygon and Star use generated vertex extrema. These drawing components do not infer intrinsic measurement from geometric dimensions; layouts that require measurement need a declared box.

Each accepts one dedicated options object and returns a fresh `Path2D`; geometric option fields are numeric-only, while `createSvgPath` accepts its `d` path data as a string. Creators own no runtime resources, event registration, cache, or render state. Rectangle width and height remain signed; shape radii and size fields are nonnegative. Creator structural or numeric validation throws `RangeError` naming the offending option path, while component style resolution reports the contextual `LayoutDiagnostic` family. `createSvgPath` intentionally delegates malformed path-data failure to the browser `Path2D` constructor.

Zero corner radii keep otherwise valid geometry sharp. This feature does not add rounded Arc, Wedge, Line, HorizontalLine, or VerticalLine joins; corner behavior for Circle/Ellipse; automatic rounded clipping for arbitrary leaves; elliptical or CSS slash radii; smoothing/splines; compound/crossing stars; a generic shape registry; a retained geometry graph/cache; intrinsic geometry measurement; or per-shape memo hooks.
`@crc/physics/3d/geometry` provides pure immutable shapes and collision queries. It does not add drawing components, Three bindings, a world runtime, or a scheduler participant.

`PathGeometry` adds mutable, packed canonical geometry to the public core entry. Path and Clip accept `PathGeometry | Path2D` in `style.d`; this extends the native path-only inputs described above. Existing path creators and memoized hooks still return Path2D. Native browser context methods still require native paths.

The class supports Canvas path builders, copying, affine transforms, canonical segment editing and a read-only mutation revision. Public `toPath2D` conversion always returns a fresh snapshot; `toSvgPathData` exports absolute SVG data. CRC privately resolves an unchanged instance/revision to one native snapshot and replaces that snapshot after edits. Paint and hit/clip geometry share the same consumed snapshot. Conversion does not occur during pointer dispatch. Old root or retained-Layer generations keep their previous native paths until updated.

Geometry edits do not schedule rendering. No content-equality/hash API or SVG parser is implied. `flattenPath`, `simplifyPath`, and `subdividePath` return new geometry, with explicit accuracy/output limits. Simplification accepts polylines only and does not promise topology preservation. Singular ellipse transforms preserve traversal through explicit lines, whose turning-point stroke joins may differ from a browser's degenerate native conics.

Public evidence lives in `path-geometry.test.tsx`, `path-geometry-builders.test.ts`, `path-geometry-utilities.test.ts`, and the editable path learning example. The approved design is [mutable path geometry](../superpowers/specs/2026-09-29-path-geometry-design.md).

`ManipulationFrame` binds one writable finite box signal to a positioned local allocation. `DragHandle` is a structural listener: only participating descendant hit geometry can start a move. `ResizeHandle`, `ResizeHandles`, and `RotationHandle` retain explicit control geometry. No frame infers bounds from content. Resize and rotation controls keep CSS-pixel visual and hit geometry while their centers follow the frame. See the [component-manipulation contract](./component-manipulation-contract.md).

baselineUnits.text: Status: implemented by TFC-03 and extended by the DOM-aligned user-event delivery on 2026-08-29.

This contract assigns every event-related resource to one owner and one idempotent release path. It supplements the [user-event contract](./user-events-contract.md) and [mouse interaction contract](./mouse-interaction-contract.md): this document governs lifetime and failure isolation, while those documents govern dispatch and geometry.
`crc(canvas, scene, config)` returns a stable `CRCController` for the active mount:
ts interface CRCController { dispose(): void; }
- Updating an already-mounted Canvas returns the same controller.

- `config.signal` is a mount option: only the signal supplied when the Canvas is first mounted owns that lifetime. A signal supplied on an update is ignored. Viewport, fit, and pixel ratio follow the same mount-only rule.
- `dispose()` is synchronous and idempotent.
- `config.signal` and `dispose()` enter the same central disposal path.
- A controller or signal from an old mount cannot dispose a newer mount on the same Canvas.
- An already-aborted signal produces an immediately disposed controller and schedules no render.
- Omitting `signal` is supported; the controller still owns and removes all native listeners.
Existing callers may ignore the additive return value. Retaining a controller does not keep its disposed scene instance alive; its closure releases that ownership after the first cleanup request.
| Resource | Sole owner | Acquisition | Release trigger | Required postcondition |

| Hover/activation state | Root interaction dispatcher | Native pointer/activation input | Target removal, completed activation, root exit, or disposal | Every referenced leaf region remains live, or the state is cleared synchronously. |
